column3: NASB adds “an interval of” and “along.”
NASB renders “set before” as “submitted to” and “those esteemed” as “those who were of reputation,” and it adds “I did so.”
NASB adds “though.”
NASB follows the critical text (future “will enslave”); “brought in secretly” is rendered “had sneaked in,” and “freedom” is “liberty.”
NASB renders “continue” as “remain.”
NASB follows the critical text; it puts the aside in parentheses and renders “God does not take the face of a man” as “God shows no partiality.”
NASB renders “of the uncircumcision” as “to the uncircumcised.”
NASB puts the verse in parentheses and renders “worked in” as “effectually worked for.”
NASB renders “esteemed to be pillars” as “reputed to be pillars.”
NASB adds “They … asked us.”
NASB reads “Cephas,” as the critical text does; “to his face” is rendered “to his face.”
NASB renders “was drawing back” as “began to withdraw” and “was separating himself” as “hold himself aloof.”
NASB renders “acted hypocritically with him” as “joined him in hypocrisy.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Cephas”); “walking uprightly” is rendered “straightforward,” and “to Judaize” is “to live like Jews.”
NASB renders “by birth” as “by nature.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Christ Jesus”); “faith from” is rendered “faith in.”
NASB renders “Never would it be” as “May it never be.”
NASB adds “once.”
NASB ends the verse at “live to God” and moves “I have been crucified with Christ” into v. 20.
NASB begins with “I have been crucified with Christ,” moved from v. 19; it follows the critical text (“the Son of God”), and “faith from” is rendered “faith in.”
NASB renders “set aside” as “nullify” and “for naught” as “needlessly.”
